rows.description: My parent takes my tablet and I feel furious and cheated. Underneath, I am upset at losing something fun. Negotiating a fixed schedule is better than sneaking screens.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, compassion, dependence, disillusionment, shame
related mind states: playfulness, anger, resentment

rows.description: My mother says I look tired and stares at my screen habit. She is worried, not being mean. Listening to her and setting a limit together shows I can take care of myself.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, dependence, disillusionment, resentment, shame

rows.description: When I am bored I grab the phone and scroll. Boredom is where new ideas begin; sometimes I can try drawing, playing outside or reading instead.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, compassion, dependence, disillusionment, resentment, shame

rows.description: My brother and I fight over the TV remote. Taking turns with a timer, or asking a parent to decide, is fairer than shouting or grabbing.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, dependence, disillusionment, resentment, shame

rows.description: My friends only want to play online now and I feel lonely if I do not join. I can invite them to play outside, and notice how I feel after long screen time.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, compassion, disillusionment, resentment, shame

rows.description: I watched something I knew I should not, and I feel embarrassed. Curiosity is normal; telling a trusted adult helps me understand what I saw and feel safe again, without being punished for asking.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, compassion, dependence, disillusionment, resentment
related mind states: shame, embarrassment, curiosity, trust

rows.description: My grandfather says we children never talk to him because of phones. I feel guilty. Putting the phone away for a story-time chat gives us both something we need.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, compassion, dependence, resentment, shame

rows.description: My dog has died and I cannot stop crying. The hole in my chest is real grief. Crying, talking and making a small memory box are healthy ways to say goodbye.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: comfort, guilt

rows.description: My father hugs me and says it is okay to cry. I feel less alone. I learn that being sad is normal and that sharing it makes the load lighter.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: grief, guilt

rows.description: A friend says, it is only a dog, get a new one. It stings because my pet was family. I can tell him gently that I need time, and turn to people who understand.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: comfort, grief, guilt
